title: VAWS Federated Knowledge Document v2
$comment: Every object in this schema sets additionalProperties:false on purpose. The schema IS the egress whitelist: a field that is not declared here cannot leave a contributing fork. Widening any object is a privacy decision, not a formatting decision.

layer.description: Must agree with the corpus directory holding this file. corpus/verified/ may only contain layer=verified.

constraint.$comment: One applicability dimension. There is no 'omitted' state: an entry must either bound the dimension or explicitly claim independence from it. An 'any' claim must state its basis, because unexamined independence claims are the usual root cause of contradictory knowledge between forks.

basis.description: Why this fact is believed independent of this dimension. Reviewed as a claim, not as prose.

values.description: Exact set of values this fact was established on.

range.description: Inclusive bounds. null means unbounded on that side, which is a claim about untested territory and should be justified in the rule body.

scope.$comment: The applicability coordinate. All dimensions are required so that 'undeclared' is not representable. Conflict resolution between forks works by diffing these coordinates.

topology.description: Parallel topology descriptors, e.g. tp8, dp4, ep16, multinode, single-node.

component.description: Owning subsystem, e.g. service-bootstrap, ssh-transport, attention-kernel, hccl.

concrete_environment.$comment: The single environment the fact was actually observed on. Unlike scope, these are exact strings, not constraints. This is what makes a verified claim auditable.

evidence.$comment: Evidence must be a reference, never prose. Prose that reads like evidence but cannot be followed is worse than no evidence.

contributor.description: GitHub handle of the submitter, or 'anonymous'.

origin_repo.description: Fork this entry was exported from, e.g. owner/vllm-ascend-workspace.

redaction_profile.description: Version of the source-side redaction ruleset applied at export. Lets the main repo re-scan the corpus when the ruleset tightens.

verified_by.description: Handles that confirmed the claim. A review bot is never a valid value here, and the submitter alone is not sufficient for layer=verified.

last_verified_at.description: Deliberately separate from lifecycle.updated_at: rewording an entry is not re-verifying it.

resolved_by.$comment: A fixed failure signature is marked resolved, not deleted. Deleting it strands everyone still on the affected versions.

conflict.$comment: Two forks asserting opposite things about the same coordinate is normally not a disagreement about facts; it is an incomplete coordinate. Conflicts are recorded as undeclared dimensions so that the fix is coordinate refinement, not arbitration. Same confounder logic as the experiment ledger.

fingerprints.description: Lowercase observable signatures used for retrieval matching.

measurement_quantity.$comment: One claimed quantity. `value` is a decimal STRING and never a JSON number, on purpose. content_hash is a byte-level agreement between implementations in several languages, and float serialization is precisely where those disagree: 2.70336 may render as 2.7033600000000001, and a trailing .0 may or may not survive. docs/federation.md step 0 forbids coercing types rather than picking a float format, so the only safe representation of a measured number in a hashed payload is the exact decimal text the measurement produced.

name.description: Stable identifier of the quantity, e.g. fp16_dense_matmul_peak. Together with `basis` this is the quantity identity that duplicate and conflict detection keys on.

basis.description: declared: the vendor states it outright (core count, clock). theoretical: derived from declared constants (a peak). measured: observed on hardware by the stated method. sustained: an observed fraction of a theoretical peak. A theoretical and a sustained claim about the same physical thing are different quantities and must never be compared as if they were the same number.

unit.description: Lowercase unit token. Canonical tokens in use: tflops, tops, gbps, gib, mhz, bytes_per_cycle, count, ratio. Lowercase is enforced so that TFLOPS and tflops cannot become two incomparable units for the same quantity.

qualifier.description: What narrows the quantity, e.g. 'dense matmul, cube 16x16x16'. Not part of the quantity identity.

measurement_subject.$comment: What the quantity is about. Deliberately a closed set of named fields rather than a free-form attribute map: the schema is the egress whitelist, and a free-form map would let an arbitrary key leave a fork.

id.description: Canonical identifier of the hardware the claim is about, e.g. Ascend910B4. Duplicate and conflict detection keys on this together with scope.

aliases.description: Other names the same hardware is sold or reported under. Aliases are for retrieval; they are not identity.

measurement_parameter.$comment: A method parameter as a name/value pair rather than a map entry, for the same egress-whitelist reason as measurement_subject: a mapping with free keys would publish keys nobody declared.

measurement_source.$comment: The artifact that produced the number. Unlike verification.evidence this is part of the claim, not part of the review record: swap the artifact and it is a different claim, so it belongs inside the hashed payload.

ref.description: A followable reference with no whitespace: a vendor file path, a manifest id, owner/repo#N, a sha, or a URL. Prose is not a reference.

measurement.$comment: The second entry body. A measurement claims a quantity about a subject, established by a stated method, at the coordinate in `scope`. It carries no symptom, root cause or resolution because a number has none; forcing one would produce invented prose in the fields review reads most carefully. A quantity the method did not establish is simply absent: absence means unknown, exactly as it does for a query that returns nothing.

summary.description: One line naming subject and claim. Populated for both body variants so a reader that only knows `rule` still gets a true sentence.

type.description: vendor_platform_config: read out of a vendor-shipped configuration snapshot. microbenchmark: timed on hardware by the described procedure.

description.description: What was done, in enough detail to repeat it. This is load-bearing evidence, not colour: it is what makes the number checkable.

reference_source.$comment: Where the sourced material came from. A URL/title/provider is a citation, not a run_manifest. version and date are the publisher's, when known.

url.description: Followable http(s) URL with no whitespace.

reference.$comment: The third entry body: sourced reference material (official documentation, a principle, or a practical guide). It is not operational evidence. It must not carry a hardware verification record or the twelve runtime coordinates; optional topics/published versions live here instead.

kind.description: What kind of sourced material this is.

summary.description: One line naming the document and the claim it supports.

text.description: Substantive attributed summary. Do not paste a full article.

trust.description: Explicit source/trust assessment. Must not claim local hardware or runtime verification.

topics.description: Optional applicable topics or published versions. Not the twelve runtime coordinates.

uuid.description: Stable identity across revisions and across forks. Never derived from content.

slug.description: Human-readable handle. Mutable, and never used as identity.

content_hash.description: Version identity over the canonicalized payload. Rule and measurement hash scope + body keyed by the body's own name. A sourced reference hashes the reference body only (no invented runtime scope). Makes federated sync idempotent per entry.

redaction_cleared_under.$comment: Main-repo owned, and deliberately separate from provenance.redaction_profile. That field records which ruleset cleared the entry at export time and is an immutable historical fact; this one records the highest ruleset the entry has since been re-scanned clean under. Without the split, a passing re-scan has nowhere to record its result, so the same entries are re-scanned forever and a published snapshot's profile floor can never rise above the oldest export. Not part of the content_hash payload: it describes how the entry was processed, not what it claims. A fork must not set it.

allOf.$comment: An entry has exactly one body. rule and measurement remain runtime claims and still require the twelve-dimension scope. reference is sourced material: it must not invent those coordinates or carry a hardware verification record.
verified and stale both assert the claim was once actually established, so both need a full verification record. stale only means it has not been re-verified recently enough.
A resolved signature must point at what fixed it, otherwise consumers cannot tell whether they are past it.
high confidence is reserved for claims that survived review, not for confident writing.
